Article Title: 'Could no longer defend the indefensible': Former AAP spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joins Congress
Article Text:
Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress. (IANS)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Aam Aadmi Party(AAP) spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday, saying she could no longer defend the “indefensible”.Explaining her decision to leave AAP, Kakkar said, “There was a time when it was said that AAP would not take a bungalow or a car. But later, choppers started being used for private travel, and I could no longer defend the indefensible. ”“I drew a line when I saw that the Aam Aadmi Party, which at one point had attracted people with great substance and intelligence, was unable to retain them,” she added.She also questioned the appointment of people to senior positions in Punjab. “Who are the people being brought in now? New people who have not even worked at the booth level are being brought from Rajasthan and given senior positions in Punjab, along with bungalows and cars,” Kakkar said.“How long can I defend the indefensible?” she added.Kakkar also praised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , calling him resilient and saying she had seen him and the party withstand attacks.“If there is one leader who is not afraid to promote his ideas, it is Rahul Gandhi. I observed that he is the only leader who has not shed tears for the cameras. He is the only leader today who has not done that. He is resilient. I have seen how he was humiliated and how an entire machinery was deployed to put him down.But Rahul Gandhi and the Congress remained resilient,” she said.“Their authenticity is their soul. I saw that there is a soul in this party as well, which I found missing in other parties. And I say this from lived experience,” she added.Kakkar also backed Rahul Gandhi's criticism of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over electoral-roll revision and his allegations concerning voters' rights.“I also saw how Rahul Gandhi has continuously launched a campaign against traitor Gyanesh Kumar. He has made everyone, including us, aware of this issue,” Kakkar said.“We have to make the public aware of how, according to him, our only voting right is being stolen by Gyanesh Kumar and put into PM Modi's account. This has to stop. Therefore, we must all come together now to support the Congress and support Rahul Gandhi in his authentic fight to keep the idea of India alive,” she added.Kakkar later called for opposition unity and urged people to join the Congress.“Now, we all have to come under one umbrella so that no votes are divided or scattered, because, as 'traitor' Gyanesh Kumar is already stealing votes and putting them into PM Modi's account. We must not give them any more opportunities. Everyone must come under one umbrella, under the Congress, to defeat PM Modi and his regressive politics,” she said.The Congress also said in a post on X that three prominent figures had joined the party, including, Priyanka Kakkar, former Uttar Pradesh MLA Shyam Sundar Sharma and journalist Rajat Rakesh Tandon.
Article Summary: Former Aam Aadmi Party spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar joined the Congress on Saturday. Kakkar said she could no longer defend the ‘indefensible’ Kakkar also praised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi calling him resilient and saying she had seen him and the party withstand attacks.

Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 132 53 45 230 2 Japan 41 68 63 172 3 South Korea 21 26 43 90 4 Uzbekistan 12 17 13 42 5 Kazakhstan 9 13 23 45 6 Thailand 9 8 13 30 7 Bahrain 9 2 3 14 8 Iran 8 15 9 32 9 North Korea 7 5 5 17 10 Malaysia 6 3 9 18 11 Hong Kong 5 12 17 34 12 INDIA 4 20 21 45

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: 'I am Hanuman to Rahul Gandhi': Ajay Rai after being replaced as UP Congress chief
Article Text:
Rai made the remarks after the Congress appointed Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ as the new UP Congress president

NEW DELHI: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) president Ajay Rai on Saturday called himself a “Hanuman” to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , saying he would continue to follow the party’s national leadership and carry out its political fight regardless of the position he holds."Whatever decision the national leadership makes. They told me to fight Modi, and I fought openly with full strength, and I will continue to fight. So whatever the national leadership decides, I stand by it. I am certainly a 'Hanuman' to my leader Rahul Gandhi; wherever he says, I will be there," he told ANI.Rai also recalled his contest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Describing himself as a “simple worker”, he said he had been fielded against PM Modi with the support of the Congress leadership and Rahul Gandhi.Rai made the remarks after the Congress appointed Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ as the new UP Congress president, replacing him as part of an organisational reshuffle ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Speaking to reporters, Rai said he had always followed the decisions of the national leadership and would continue to do so."A simple worker like me was fielded against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With the support of the top leadership and Rahul Gandhi, we secured 4.6 lakh votes in Varanasi and defeated PM Modi in seven rounds. I thank Rahul Gandhi and the top leadership for their faith in me and extend my best wishes to Aradhana Mishra Mona. I hope she works hard, takes the party forward and strengthens the trust of workers by standing with them against oppression and injustice," he said.Rai said political positions were temporary and pointed to his record as a five-time MLA from Pindra. He said he had worked extensively for people in his constituency and recalled arranging blood donations when required."Positions in politics come and go. I have been an MLA from Pindra five times and have worked extensively for the people, even arranging blood donations through my family when needed. I thank the Pradesh Congress Committee employees, drivers, staff, workers and supporters who stood by me around the clock and helped me throughout my journey across Uttar Pradesh. We have always stood against oppression and injustice wherever it occurred," he said.Meanwhile, Mishra, after taking charge as the new UP Congress president, said the party was ready for the 2027 Assembly elections and would contest them with the INDIA alliance."Today marks the beginning of a new dawn. I express my gratitude to my leadership for entrusting me with this responsibility. This is a big challenge; time is short, and every Congress worker will have to work. Together, we must work with full strength," she said.Mishra also highlighted the Congress’ focus on women’s empowerment, saying, "If there's anyone who is the biggest example of 'Beti Hun, Lad Sakti Hun', it is me."She recalled the party’s decision under Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s leadership to field 40% women candidates in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections."Before this, under Priyanka Gandhi's leadership, we fielded 40% women candidates with tickets in the 2022 elections. It is evident today that the Congress Party has always worked for the empowerment of women," she said."We are ready for the 2027 elections, and the INDIA alliance will contest the elections with full strength. We will fight the elections with the entire alliance," the newly appointed UP Congress chief said.
Article Summary: Rai made the remarks after the Congress appointed Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ as the new UP Congress president. He also recalled his contest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Mishra also highlighted the Congress’ focus on women’s empowerment.

Article Title: Warring out, Pargat Singh in: Has Congress solved Punjab crisis or created more confusion?
Article Text:
Amrinder Raja Warring, Pargat SIngh

Warring is out, but not down

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring hints that Sachin Pilot may have played a role in his exit.

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said he stepped down as Punjab Congress chief after reading the 'direction of the wind'

How the Channi-Warring tussle began

Warring out, but Channi not in

2022 rerun in Punjab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The churn in Punjab Congress is now complete. Or is it?Amarinder Singh Raja Warring is out and Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress president. The change came hours after Warring resigned from the post, ending his more than four-year stint as state party chief. Warring met Rahul Gandhi on Friday and formally submitted his resignation. A day earlier, he had changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President”, signalling the leadership change."He (Rahul Gandhi) gave me a lot of love. He sought information about the current political situation in Punjab, on what is happening with the government and what we should be doing there," Warring said after his meeting.Hours later, the Congress announced the appointment of Pargat Singh as the new Punjab Congress president with immediate effect. The party also appreciated the contribution of outgoing president Warring.The change in Punjab Congress comes after months of infighting over who should lead the Congress into the 2027 assembly election. The crisis was triggered by Congress’s decision to retain Warring as state unit president in July, ignoring the claims of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi . So, Warring’s exit marks a victory for Channi and his supporters, but the entry of Pargat Singh means he does not gain from Warring's loss.Warring may be out of his post, but has dropped strong hints that his fight may be far from over. Hours after formally stepping down, Warring targeted his detractors, signalling he is not leaving the field yet. If Warring’s remarks against party incharge Sachin Pilot are an indication to go by, we could well see a reversal of roles in Punjab Congress infighting.In an interaction with news agency ANI, Warring said, “I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove ‘Raja’ from the post.” Warring, though, added that he had “no concrete proof” of this.Warring added he had not spoken to Pilot about his exit, but had heard that the state Congress incharge may have recommended a change. “Perhaps the in-charge mentioned that Raja Warring would have to be replaced,” he said when asked about the reasons for his resignation.Taking digs at those responsible for his exit, Warring said nobody had formally asked him to resign. Instead, he had simply read the “direction of the wind”."Just like elder women who could tell by reading the direction of the wind whether it was going to rain... I observed the situation closely, and it never reached the point where someone had to ask me to resign," Warring told IANS.That, he said, was why he changed his X bio to “Former PPCC President” even before formally submitting his resignation to Rahul Gandhi.The timing and the turn of events are hard to miss. Nearly a month ago, Congress removed former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel as Punjab in-charge after the Channi faction openly rebelled against him. Baghel was accused of favouring Warring and was eventually replaced by Sachin Pilot.But now, Warring appears ready to open a front against Pilot and, of course, also Channi.That also raises questions about whether replacing Baghel with Pilot has actually helped Congress settle the Punjab crisis. Sugata Srinivasaraju, senior political analyst and author, believes that the leadership change appears to have created more confusion rather than resolving the crisis at hand."What is it that the Congress saw in Pilot that they did not see in Baghel? If you thought Baghel was part of the problem, now Pilot has also become part of the problem. He’s not part of the solution," he said.According to him, Congress may now have ended up with an even bigger problem. "All of them were against Warring. Now Warring goes out and Channi has not been catered to. So we don't know what's going to happen."Both Baghel and Warring are now out of their roles in Punjab Congress. For the Channi camp, it means one of their biggest demands has been met. But with Pargat Singh in the chair, will today's change end weeks of internal feud and bickering in Punjab Congress? Perhaps not.To understand why Warring’s exit and Pargat's entry may not be the end of the crisis, it helps to go back to where the tussle began.The crisis began on July 1, when the Congress leadership announced that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress president and Channi would head the campaign committee. Senior leaders Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Vijay Inder Singla were also given specific roles for the 2027 assembly election.On paper, it looked like an attempt to balance competing camps. In practice, it did the opposite.Channi’s supporters questioned why Warring was being retained as state chief and began pushing for a larger role for the former chief minister. What was meant to settle the leadership question instead reopened old faultlines within the party.Warring had been appointed Punjab Congress president after the party’s crushing defeat to AAP in the 2022 assembly election. Channi had been the party’s chief ministerial face in that campaign but lost both seats he contested.Warring was then brought in by the Congress high command (read Rahul Gandhi) to rebuild the organisation and prepare it for the next election. For nearly four years, however, the Congress did not clearly announce who would lead its 2027 campaign.When it finally tried to do that in July, the compromise pleased no one.Bhupesh Baghel, who was then Punjab in-charge, tried to defuse the tussle between the Channi and Warring camps but was also caught in the crossfire and forced out of the state.His replacement, Sachin Pilot, initially managed to bring the rival factions onto the same stage during the Congress protest over the Gulzar Singh suicide case. But that show of unity did not last long.What followed was another round of meetings, complaints and feedback to the high command and, eventually, Warring's exit and Pargat's entry.The Congress high command acted swiftly after Warring's exit and handed over the baton to Pargat Singh. The three-time Congress MLA from Jalandhar Cantt and former Indian hockey captain who has served as Punjab cabinet minister in Charanjit Singh Channi cabinet, has his task cut out.Pargat's name was doing the rounds along with other key contenders which included, former MLA Rana KP Singh, Raja Sansi MLA Sukhbinder Singh Sarkaria, former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa. But the frontrunner before today's appointment was former PWD minister and MP Vijay Inder Singla, who was appointed chairperson of the Congress Election Management and Coordination Committee in the July reshuffle."I am a loyal soldier of the party, and at all times, as a worker of the party, whatever responsibility I have been given, I have always fulfilled my duties. And in the coming times as well, we will work together with everyone in the same manner," Singla had said earlier reacting to speculations that he could replace Warring.However that did not happen.And this is where the leadership change in Punjab Congress becomes more interesting.The Channi camp had openly demanded that the former CM should lead the party into the next elections. In fact, their contention all along was that Warring should be replaced by Channi. But today's announcement would leave them disappointed much like the other contenders including Singla.With the Congress picking up Pargat Singh as the compromise candidate, it is a rerun of what happened in the run up to the 2022 elections.And that brings Punjab Congress back to a very familiar problem of bitter power tussle between state leaders. A problem that played a key role in the party’s defeat in 2022.Ahead of the 2022 assembly election, then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and Navjot Singh Sidhu were locked in a bitter leadership battle. Sidhu wanted a bigger role in leading the party into the election, while Amarinder resisted attempts to cut into his authority.The Congress leadership allowed the dispute to drag on until the crisis became impossible to contain. Eventually, Amarinder Singh was removed as chief minister. Charanjit Singh Channi emerged as the compromise candidate of Congress high command and was made the chief minister.But the compromise did not end the factional war. Congress went into the election divided and suffered a historic defeat, with AAP sweeping into power.Four years later, the names have changed, but the problem looks strikingly similar.Srinivasaraju sees a larger pattern in Punjab Congress's repeated leadership tussles."Punjab Congress has not been able to resolve it at all. They've had five long years after Amarinder Singh’s exit and they have still not got it right," he said.His argument is that every time Congress begins to see a chance of returning to power in Punjab, competing factions become more active and start weakening the organisation from within."We have seen that with Navjot Singh Sidhu and Amarinder Singh," he said, adding that similar mistakes "seem to be getting repeated".Once again, both the rival leaders - Channi and Warring - are out. But the battle for Channi is still half won. And with Warring all set for a rebel role, the road ahead for the former Punjab chief minister may not be easy.With Warring’s loss not translating into Channi's gain, it will be interesting to see if the Congress's compromise candidate ends this leadership fight once and for all without starting another power tussle?
Article Summary: Pargat Singh is the new Punjab Congress president. Amrinder Raja Warring resigned from the post, ending his more than four-year stint as state party chief. Warring may be out of his post, but has dropped strong hints that his fight may be far from over.

Article Title: The average will never applaud the exceptional
Article Text:
The Final Problem’

“Venmai Enappaduvadhu Yaadhenin, Onmai

Udayam Yaam Ennum Serukku.”

“What is mediocrity? It is the vanity that declares, ‘I am wise.’”

A doctor by profession, Arthur Conan Doyle travelled to the Arctic, supported the early use of vaccines when they were still viewed with apprehension, and wrote poetry, drama, history and fiction. He was also an enthusiastic sportsman and introduced skiing in Switzerland’s Alps mountains.But none of these achievements would define his place in popular imagination as the creation of one character: Sherlock Holmes.Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. Doyle gave him a mind of extraordinary precision.There were interesting contradictions between the author and the character he created. Holmes does not believe in ghosts, but Doyle deeply believed in conversations with spirits!Some of the quotations by Holmes are intense and sets you to think. “There is nothing more deceptive than an obvious fact.” “When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth.” And, with characteristic arrogance, he declares, “I am my brain, the rest of me is merely an appendix.”Doyle eventually grew frustrated that Holmes had overshadowed everything else he had written. So, in ‘, published in 1893, he killed Holmes, sending him and his arch-rival Professor Moriarty plunging to their deaths at the Reichenbach Falls.The readers could not accept this.There was outrage and thousands of cancellations of magazine subscriptions. Doyle had underestimated the bond between Holmes and his readers. Eventually he resurrected him in another story.Among Holmes’s many quotations, one particularly catches my attention:“Mediocrity knows nothing higher than itself. But talent instantly recognises genius.”There is something profound in both halves of that sentence.Mediocrity is not necessarily a lack of talent, nor is something to be looked down upon. The danger lies elsewhere: when comfort becomes a reason not to acknowledge efforts of others. The word mediocrity has a Latin root that means – ‘halfway up the mountain’.Perhaps that is why the mediocre mind often struggles to acknowledge greatness. When someone spends years pursuing a mission; a writer writing, an artist creating, an entrepreneur building, a reformer changing, there may be someone who asks, “But he did not make any money” or “She did not take care of her family”. Lest they understand that the pursuit for greatness is fulfilling in itself.And that is where the second half of Holmes’s observation becomes even more powerful.‘Talent recognises genius’.Helen Keller, deaf and blind, met M S Subbulakshmi when she visited India in 1955. When MS began to sing, Keller gently placed her fingers on the singer’s throat, sensing the vibrations of the music. Deeply moved, she is remembered for telling MS, “You sing like an angel.”How beautifully one extraordinary person spotted another.Long before Holmes, Thiruvalluvar had captured the human weakness of mediocrity with astonishing precision. In Kural 844, he says:The mountain does not become smaller because someone has stopped climbing.And greatness may simply be the courage to keep looking upward.
Article Summary: Holmes became legendary because he was more than a detective. He observed what others overlooked, questioned what others accepted and followed reason where intuition might have led people astray. The word mediocrity has a Latin root that means – ‘halfway up the mountain’

Article Title: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR
Article Text:
An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 'deleted' voters.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive completed in 20 states, besides facilitating first-time or young electors.As part of the drive - meant to percolate to the grassroots the message that the deletions made during SIR, if erroneous, can be undone at any time by simply filling up Form 6 (for fresh enrolment) - booth level officers (BLOs) will visit homes of electors who were there in the pre-SIR electoral roll but were not included in the current electoral roll. They will, during these visits, ascertain the present status of such electors and facilitate their enrolment through Form 6, wherever a person is found to be eligible. This could be due to a valid eligibility proof not submitted earlier, corrected mapping to roll from last SIR, return of a shifted voter at registered address, or a young voter who has turned 18 since SIR, etc, said an official."Voter enrolment is a continuous process and any person not yet enrolled in the electoral roll or whose name has got deleted can apply for enrolment at any point of time. The objective of the special drive is to identify and facilitate such electors," EC said in a letter to state chief electoral officers (CEOs) Thursday.This followed a meeting held by EC with state/UT CEOs on Tuesday.As per the decision taken by the full commission on Sept 26, no declaration will need to be attached with Form 6 during the special drive.Nearly 7.7 crore voters were deleted across 13 states covered in SIR's first two phases, though net deletions came to around 5.6 crore. In Phase 3, completed in seven states, net deletions total nearly 24 lakh.The special drive's timing is significant as it comes days after a report in The Indian Express report alleged that election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised questions over the SIR process in internal notes. However, the EC, in a statement released after a full commission meeting on Sept 26, placed it on record that all decisions related to SIR were unanimously approved by the CEC and the commissioners.The opposition, however, continues to amplify the issue, "unilaterally" blaming CEC Gyanesh Kumar for a "flawed" SIR, "unauthorised" changes to Form 6 and allegedly limited access of field officers to ECINet for making changes.Sources in the EC, however, told TOI Friday that the special drive is only in furtherance of the repeated directions by CEC to BLOs that "not a single Indian citizen who has completed 18 years of age should be left out of electoral roll".An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 "deleted" voters. With the EC instructing BLOs on Friday to visit the homes of 20-25 electors per week, house-to-house outreach and verification is expected to last a month.BLOs who visit the houses of deleted electors shall indicate the present status of each such elector in a list of absent, permanently shifted, deceased, duplicate and foreigner electors prepared by them. Electors for whom Form 6 has been filled up will also be indicated.They will share this list with booth level agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties and with electoral registration officers (EROs), along with the filled-up Form 6 and their field verification report. ERO is the competent authority to decide on addition or deletion.At the end of this exercise, the booth-wise lists prepared as above will also be shared by the EROs with the representatives of the political parties, giving them a further opportunity to enable enrolment of any left-out electors.Booth-level camps shall be organised to facilitate submission of applications for enrolment. Special camps may also be organised for enrolment of people living in night shelters, labour colonies and also for homeless & marginalised persons.As part of SIR completed in 20 states, a list of ASDD voters was prepared by each BLO with the probable reason for non-inclusion of their names. This list was displayed at the notice board of respective panchayat bhawans/urban local bodies and offices of the BDOs/panchayat, shared with the BLAs and with the political parties and also uploaded on the CEO website.Thereafter, the draft was published and shared with the political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. The final electoral roll was published after decisions on the claims and objections by the EROs and includes the list of electors that were added or deleted after the draft publication.
Article Summary: The Election Commission on Thursday ordered a special drive to identify and add back genuine electors who may have been "left out" during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) drive completed in 20 states. An EC official said an average 10% of 800-900 electors per booth were deleted through SIR. Thus, each BLO will have to verify enrolment eligibility of less than 100 'deleted' voters.

Article Title: India’s diversity, traditional knowledge can help build better world: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat
Article Text:

Bhagwat on common thread in different traditions

‘Identity of Bharat’ should reach next generation

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Friday said Bharat’s identity was rooted in its diversity of languages, faiths, castes and cultures, and that the country could contribute to building a better world by combining its traditional knowledge with modern progress.Addressing a gathering at Prabhadevi in Mumbai, Bhagwat said the younger generation should be taught about Indian society and its traditions while also drawing on knowledge from across the world for the betterment of society.Bhagwat recalled an interaction at an interfaith meeting where a participant told him that religious conflicts were causing loss of human lives but that a solution to the problem was not readily available.“He asked me to come to his country and spread the teachings and knowledge of Bharat to the world,” Bhagwat said.The RSS chief said the eternal knowledge contained in the Bhagavad Gita was reflected in various traditions in India and elsewhere, although the expressions and words differed depending on the time and circumstances.“The conclusion of various philosophies, from ancient traditions to the latest one, is the same.From the ancient period of human beings who wondered about the world till Yuval Noah Harari (Israeli medievalist and historian), the range of thoughts and their conclusions are the same,” he said.People need to understand eternal truth to understand the world, their surroundings and how they should conduct themselves, Bhagwat said.He added that different traditions may use different expressions to communicate the same fundamental principles and that people should focus on the direction of those teachings rather than merely their outward expressions.“If you ignore the message and only focus on the choice of words, it creates confusion,” he said.Bhagwat also referred to scientific studies on consciousness and said, “Today, the world has one common consciousness. It is the beginning of everything. Everything started by a pre-existing universal consciousness.”He compared the intellect to a driver, the soul to the owner and the different parts of the body to the horses of a chariot. Ego, he said, could sometimes misdirect a person and lead to sorrow and disappointment, making guidance important when dealing with challenges in life.“With a minor disappointment, people get frustrated and some even end their lives. If you want to do daily things, you need guidance. Those who have lived life like that have told us,” he said.Bhagwat said great personalities and their works provided guidance to society, helping people preserve their values while adapting to changing circumstances.Speaking about the youth, he said members of Gen Z who go abroad are often reminded that their origins lie in Bharat, its traditions and knowledge. People want them to explain the country’s specialities and identity, he added.Bhagwat recalled an example shared by a participant who described Bharat as an impressive country after visiting a state-of-the-art oil refinery in Jamnagar, Gujarat.Amid the activity at the refinery, the participant noticed a huge idol of Lord Ganesha and remarked, “That is Bharat”, Bhagwat said.“This is the identity of Bharat and we have a sense of pride in it. It should be passed on to the next generation,” he said.The RSS chief said the younger generation should be taught how to face upcoming challenges, continue moving forward regardless of success or failure and make their lives meaningful.Bhagwat also noted that it was often said that members of the new generation did not have a strong command over their mother tongue and that the attention span of the current generation was also shorter.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat: Bharat's identity is rooted in its diversity of languages, faiths, castes and cultures. He said the country could contribute to building a better world by combining its traditional knowledge with modern progress. The RSS chief said the eternal knowledge contained in the Bhagavad Gita was reflected in various traditions.

Article Title: Akhilesh Yadav's Rajya Sabha picks: Samajwadi Party's master strategy or 'PDA' contradiction?
Article Text:
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has nominated Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha polls.

Why Nathwani?

The third nomination suspense

A rehearsal for 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A 'family' man, a corporate executive, a possible third candidate and a high-stakes numbers game: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav 's Rajya Sabha strategy has a bit of a test run for the 2027 UP assembly polls?His two picks have an element of continuity and also surprise. But then there is also an element of contradiction vis-à-vis the strong PDA pitch which has been the backbone of his 2027 poll strategy. Little wonder, then, that talk of a third nominee has begun even without the numbers, raising the stakes from a routine Rajya Sabha contest to an early test of Akhilesh's 2027 strategy.For the two sure-shot Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav has paired a familiar Samajwadi Party face with a distinctly unfamiliar political profile. Alongside his uncle Ram Gopal Yadav, the SP has nominated Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, a senior Reliance Industries executive whose father, Parimal Nathwani, is a four-time Rajya Sabha MP backed by the BJP-led NDA. The choice immediately puts two very different images of the SP on the same ticket: its established family name and a corporate, professional profile from outside its traditional ecosystem.Nathwani's nomination also raises a larger question about the SP's direction as it prepares for the 2027 assembly election.Is Nathwani's nomination an attempt to expand the SP's political appeal beyond its traditional social base, or does bringing a senior corporate executive into Parliament sit uneasily with a party increasingly building its politics for the 2027 polls around PDA, Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak? The question matters beyond the Rajya Sabha because the SP is simultaneously trying to project itself as the principal challenger to the BJP in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 assembly election.Akhilesh's second nomination is more than a surprise name on a candidate list. His corporate background gives the SP an opportunity to make a political argument it has not traditionally foregrounded. The party can present his candidature as evidence that its appeal is extending beyond its conventional political base and that people from the corporate and professional world now see the party as a credible political force.For a party preparing for 2027, that can also help reinforce a broader pitch around investment, jobs, industry and development alongside its social-justice agenda, which could become a significant part of the BJP and Yogi government's election campaign next year.Akhilesh, in fact, responded to queries over criticism of Nathwani's nomination by invoking Ram Manohar Lohia. "I think you should read about socialism again. I will give you a book by (Ram Manohar) Lohia," he said. He argued that socialist thought also talks about prosperity and equality and said governments across the country seek investment to generate economic growth."This time, it will be Lodhi vs Yogi (Adityanath)," he said on September 30.However, the same choice also produces a very different political reading.Akhilesh's electoral strategy for the 2027 polls has been heavily identified with PDA, and Nathwani is not an obvious representative of the social coalition that phrase describes. That gives the opposition an opening to question why a party seeking votes in the name of backward classes, Dalits and minorities has chosen a senior corporate executive for one of its two Rajya Sabha seats.Mayawati, in fact, used the same charge against the SP. "SP wants votes in the name of PDA, but makes mostly its own family members and big capitalists MPs and MLAs," she said in a post on X.State minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar also targeted Akhilesh, accusing him of repeatedly changing the framework for PDA. "Akhilesh Yadav keeps changing the PDA formula from time to time. Yesterday, he came up with the formula of a PDA family. 'P' now stands for 'Parivaar'," Rajbhar said, referring to Ram Gopal Yadav. "‘D’ stands for the 'Daulat', referring to Dhani Ram, who is affluent," Rajbhar said."Now, only 'A' remains, and he will bring in some criminal to represent it. The new PDA formula stands for 'Parivaar', 'Daulat' and 'Apradhi'," he added.The BJP, meanwhile, is watching Nathwani's nomination closely but has not mounted a similarly strong direct attack on the choice.The Uttar Pradesh assembly currently has 396 effective members after seven vacancies, putting the winning quota for a Rajya Sabha seat at 37 first-preference votes. The BJP has 255 MLAs, while the SP has 101 and Congress has two. The BJP's alliance partners include Apna Dal (S), RLD, SBSP and Nishad Party, giving the ruling camp a substantial numerical advantage. Broadly, the BJP-led camp is positioned to take the larger share of the 10 seats, while the SP-Congress combination has enough strength for two.The problem begins with the third candidate. The SP would need roughly nine additional first-preference votes to reach the quota for a third seat. That means Akhilesh cannot rely only on his existing alliance strength. He would have to attract support from outside it, potentially through smaller parties, independents or legislators willing to cross-vote.The suspense over that third candidate has now become central to the contest. SP MP Virendra Singh has said the party will field a third candidate, with the name to be decided and the nomination filed by October 5. Singh has also claimed that several BJP MLAs seeking SP tickets for the 2027 elections are in touch with the party.Akhilesh, meanwhile, has continued to leave room for political manoeuvring. Earlier in the day he described the Rajya Sabha election as "the time for coming together" and said it offered an opportunity to forget past mistakes and stand united with others on matters of principle.A day earlier, when asked whether the SP would field a third candidate, he declined to confirm the party's plans and said: "The BJP can do anything. They can field nine or even 10 candidates."The BJP, meanwhile, has made its own claims about SP legislators. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya has said that 25 SP MLAs are in contact with the BJP and warned that the party would "surprise" the SP.This Rajya Sabha election, along with the immediate parliamentary tally, will ultimately be about a strategic stress-test for 2027.In fielding Nathwani, Akhilesh Yadav is executing a high-stakes balancing act: attempting to reposition the Samajwadi Party as a pragmatic, investment-friendly government-in-waiting, without alienating the core PDA base that forms its electoral backbone. It is a gamble that risks handing opponents cheap ideological ammunition in exchange for broader institutional credibility and expanded corporate outreach.Whether this move is remembered as a masterstroke of political expansion or a self-inflicted ideological contradiction will not be decided in the corridors of the Rajya Sabha. It will be decided by how effectively Akhilesh manages the cross-currents - maintaining the confidence of his grassroots voters while proving that his vision for Uttar Pradesh can accommodate both social justice and corporate capital. The upcoming floor vote, and the potential fight for a third seat, will offer the first real glimpse of whether that strategy can hold.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav has nominated Ram Gopal Yadav and Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha polls. The choice immediately puts two very different images of the SP on the same ticket: its established family name and a corporate, professional profile.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Amarinder Singh Raja Warring on Friday formally resigned as the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief, handing over his resignation to Rahul Gandhi amid reports of a leadership change ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.Warring, who headed the state Congress for around four-and-a-half years, indicated that party's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may have played a role in the decision to replace him, though he said he had no concrete evidence to support his claim."Given my long journey in politics, I feel that Sachin Pilot must have decided it was time to remove 'Raja' from the post. Article Title: Gandhi's first birthday in free India was no celebration: What happened on October 2, 1947
Article Text:
Freedom was just two months old and the country was still struggling to come to terms with Partition when Gandhi’s 78th birthday approached

A country in flames

What Gandhi did on his 78th birthday

'Today nobody listens to me'

'If I’m to die by the bullet of a mad man ...'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India wanted to celebrate Mahatma Gandhi on October 2, 1947. Gandhi, however, himself wanted no celebration at all.It was his first birthday in an independent India and, as it turned out, his last. Messages, flowers and greetings poured in from India and abroad. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and others came to meet him. But Gandhi, who turned 78 that day, was consumed by what was happening outside the walls of Birla House.Barely seven weeks had passed since Independence. Partition had displaced millions and triggered widespread communal violence across India and Pakistan.So when people wished Gandhi a long life, his response was not one of celebration."Where did the congratulations come in? Would it not be more appropriate to say condolences?" he asked.Later that day, Gandhi told those gathered for his prayer meeting: "For me today is the day of mourning. I am surprised and also ashamed that I am still alive."Freedom was just two months old and the country was still struggling to come to terms with Partition when Gandhi’s 78th birthday approached.Gandhi had already spent months confronting the violence.According to the Gandhi Heritage Portal, he left for Noakhali in November 1946 after communal violence erupted there and later began a barefoot march through affected villages, appealing for peace and Hindu-Muslim unity.His peace mission continued even when India became independent. The Gandhi Heritage Portal records that Gandhi stayed in riot-hit Calcutta in August 1947 and spent Independence Day fasting and praying rather than taking part in the celebrations.Violence followed Gandhi to Delhi. According to the Gandhi Heritage Portal, when he reached the capital on September 9, 1947, communal violence and refugee camps had made it impossible for him to stay at his usual accommodation at Valmiki Colony, and he moved into Birla House instead.From there, Gandhi continued holding prayer meetings and appealing for communal peace as tensions gripped the capital.According to historian Brijmohan Heda, October 2, 1947, was remembered by those who visited Gandhi that day as one of the most painful days of his life. While the country prepared to celebrate his birthday, Gandhi showed little interest in the celebrations and spent much of the day in prayer and spinning the charkha.At the morning prayer, Mirabehn decorated the space around Gandhi’s seat at Birla House with flowers arranged in the shape of an Om, the words 'Hey Ram' and a cross. Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Ghanshyamdas Birla and Indira Gandhi were among those present.Lady Mountbatten was among those who visited Gandhi later in the day and brought letters and telegrams sent to him from India and abroad.A special radio programme had also been planned to mark his birthday. When asked whether he would listen to the All India Radio programme, Gandhi made his choice clear. He said he would give greater importance to the 'rentio', the spinning wheel, than to the radio.Later in the evening, Gandhi suffered a bout of coughing. His doctors advised him to take penicillin, but he refused, saying Ramanama: the chanting of Lord Rama’s name was his 'sole remedy'.Consumed by the bloodshed around him, Gandhi used his prayer meeting address on October 2, 1947, to speak openly about his anguish.“Today is my birthday. I do not celebrate my birthday in the usual way. I would say that on this day we must fast, spin and pray. That, in my view, is the most appropriate way of celebrating one’s birthday,” Gandhi said.“For me today is the day of mourning. I am surprised and also ashamed that I am still alive. I am the same person whose word was honoured by the millions of the country. But today nobody listens to me,” he added. The remarks are recorded in the Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi.Gandhi then spoke about the growing hostility towards Muslims and questioned what India would become if the violence continued.“You want only the Hindus to remain in India and say that none else should be left behind. You may kill the Muslims today; but what will you do tomorrow? What will happen to the Parsis and the Christians and then to the British?” he said.“Ever since I came to India I have made it my profession to work for communal harmony, and I wish that though our religions are different we may live in amity like brothers. But today we seem to have become enemies,” Gandhi said.Gandhi also said he had given up his earlier desire to live to the age of 125.“I have now stopped thinking about living for 125 years. I have stopped thinking in terms of 100 or even 90 years. I am entering my 79th year today; but even that pains me,” he said.He ended with an appeal against communal hatred: “If you really want to celebrate my birthday, it is your duty not to let anyone be possessed by madness and if there is any anger in your hearts you must remove it.”After the prayer meeting, Gandhi spoke to Sardar Patel in private and asked what “sin” he had committed to be kept alive to witness such horrors, an exchange also recounted by historian Ramachandra Guha.Just four months later, Gandhi was assassinated in New Delhi.On January 30, 1948, as he walked towards the evening prayer meeting at Birla House, Nathuram Godse approached him and fired three shots at close range. Gandhi died shortly afterwards. The Gandhi Heritage Portal records that he was shot while on his way to the prayer ground and received three bullets.Gandhi was 78 when he was killed. He had spent much of his life speaking against violence and urging Hindus and Muslims to live together peacefully.Just two days before his assassination, Gandhi had spoken about the possibility of being killed."If I’m to die by the bullet of a mad man, I must do so smiling. God must be in my heart and on my lips," he had said on January 28, 1948, according to a contemporary report published by 'The Hindu'.Four months earlier, on his last birthday, Gandhi had already spoken of losing his desire for a long life.The man who had once hoped to live for 125 years had finally seen India become independent. But on his first birthday in free India, the violence surrounding that freedom left him with little reason to celebrate.
Article Summary: October 2, 1947, was Gandhi's first birthday in an independent India. Messages, flowers and greetings poured in from India and abroad. But Gandhi was consumed by what was happening outside the walls of Birla House. Partition had displaced millions and triggered widespread communal violence across India and Pakistan.

J.J. Watt and Kealia Watt have found a way to keep sports at the center of their lives even after stepping away from professional competition. J.J. finished his NFL career as a three-time Defensive Player of the Year and one of the most recognizable defensive players of his generation, while Kealia built her own career in professional soccer and earned three appearances for the U.S. women’s national team. Today, the couple’s influence stretches from English football ownership to television and, most importantly, a charitable foundation that has funded millions of dollars in youth sports programs. Their story is not simply about what two former athletes did with their money after retirement. It is about how they turned their experience, reputation and love for sport into something with a much wider reach.J.J. Watt had already spent years thinking about what would come after football before he retired from the NFL following the 2022 season. After 12 seasons with the Houston Texans and Arizona Cardinals, he had become a three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and finished his career with 114.5 sacks. But retirement did not mean leaving professional sports behind.In May 2023, J.J. and Kealia announced that they had become minority investors in Burnley FC, the historic English club based in Lancashire.The investment came just after Burnley won the EFL Championship and secured promotion to the Premier League. The exact size of the couple’s stake and the amount they invested have not been publicly disclosed.For J.J., the move combined two interests. He had followed the Premier League for years, while Kealia brought her own professional soccer background to the decision. The couple had reportedly spent around three years looking for a club they could invest in together before choosing Burnley. J.J. also spoke with Ryan Reynolds about his experience with Wrexham, as the Watts considered how sports ownership could connect them with fans outside the United States.Their approach to Burnley has also been noticeably hands-on. Instead of treating the investment as simply another name on an ownership list, the couple spent time learning about the town, its history and its supporters. J.J. even joined fans at local pubs and community events as he tried to understand what Burnley meant to the people who had supported the club for generations.The Watts have been open about wanting to help Burnley reach more fans internationally, particularly in the United States. But they have also stressed that international growth should not come at the expense of the club’s identity.That balance is important because Burnley is not a new sports brand looking for an audience. The club dates back to 1882 and is deeply connected to the town. When the Watts announced their investment, they described themselves as investing not only in the squad and manager but also in the community around the club.Kealia’s involvement brings another dimension. Having played in the National Women’s Soccer League and for the U.S. national team, she understands the development of women’s professional soccer from the player’s side. When the couple joined Burnley’s ownership group, she specifically spoke about wanting to help with the growth of the club’s women’s team, drawing on what she had seen happen with the NWSL in the United States.J.J.’s post-NFL career has also moved into broadcasting. He joined CBS Sports as an NFL analyst in 2023, giving him another major platform outside playing football.The Burnley investment therefore fits into a much larger transition. J.J. is no longer earning his influence from sacks and defensive plays, while Kealia is no longer building her profile through goals and appearances. Instead, they are using their experience as athletes, their public profiles and their understanding of sports to take on different roles.The most measurable part of J.J. Watt’s legacy away from the NFL may be the Justin J. Watt Foundation.Founded in 2011, the foundation focuses on giving middle-school children access to after-school athletic programs. Its mission is built around more than simply getting children onto a playing field. The organization says its programs are designed to help young people develop accountability, teamwork, leadership, work ethic and perseverance in a safe and supervised environment.The scale has grown considerably. According to the foundation’s current figures, it has funded more than $7.8 million for youth athletic programs across 999 schools in 43 states and Washington, D.C. Its progress page currently lists $7,845,386.25 toward an $8 million funding goal.The money goes toward practical needs that can make a difference for school sports programs. Recent grants have helped schools purchase football equipment, soccer uniforms, wrestling mats, basketball equipment, track gear and other supplies.That makes the foundation’s work particularly easy to measure. Instead of simply announcing a broad commitment to young people, the organization provides funding for things students and schools can actually use.The foundation also has a history that extends beyond its regular youth-sports program.One of the biggest moments in J.J. Watt’s charitable career came after Hurricane Harvey struck Houston in 2017.Watt launched a fundraising campaign to help people affected by the disaster. What began with a target of $200,000 eventually grew into a campaign that raised more than $41 million for relief efforts. The funds were distributed through partner organizations working on the ground rather than simply being folded into the foundation’s normal youth-sports program.The scale of that campaign changed the way many people viewed Watt’s charitable work. He was no longer simply a professional athlete running a foundation. His public profile had become powerful enough to bring enormous attention and donations to a crisis affecting an entire community.Importantly, the Harvey campaign should not be confused with the foundation’s regular youth-athletics funding. The foundation itself explains that the Harvey money was distributed to four partner organizations before it returned its focus to after-school athletic programs.That distinction makes the Watts’ overall story more interesting, not less. Their commercial activities, sports investments and charitable work serve different purposes. Burnley is a private investment. Broadcasting is part of J.J.’s professional career. The foundation is a nonprofit focused on children and athletics.Together, however, they show how far the Watts’ influence has expanded since their playing days. They have moved from competing on football and soccer fields to owning a piece of an English club, appearing in sports media and funding opportunities for children across the United States. The foundation alone has reached hundreds of schools, while their Burnley investment has given them a new role in a sport Kealia knows from the inside.For J.J. and Kealia Watt, life after professional sports has not meant stepping away from sports. It has meant finding new ways to shape them.
Article Summary: J.J. Watt and Kealia Watt became minority investors in Burnley FC in May 2023. The couple's influence stretches from English football ownership to television and a charitable foundation. The Watt Foundation has funded millions of dollars in youth sports programs.

Article Title: Stephen Curry reveals how his wife Ayesha Curry reacted to massive $20 million pay cut in Warriors contract extension
Article Text:
Stephen and Ayesha Curry. Image via: Drew Altizer Photography/Shutterstock

Stephen Curry explains how Ayesha Curry reacted to the $20 million pay cut

Curry ties the Warriors extension to his first NBA contract

A $20 million pay cut is a hard thing to bring home. Stephen Curry took one in the Warriors extension, signing for roughly that much less than the top figure, and he had to tell his wife, Ayesha, about it.In an interview with ABC7 News Bay Area, Curry took on the idea that the decision must have been stressful. He pointed to gratitude, the odd scale of NBA money and the first contract he ever signed. Then he explained why the whole household is aligned.Stephen Curry told Ayesha he would be taking something of a pay cut for the rest of his time with the Warriors, and he later described how the conversation went to ABC7 News Bay Area. The interview was reported on Friday, October 2.What came through was agreement. When the talk turned to Ayesha and the rest of the family, Curry said "everybody's on the same page" about the part of the situation he can control. He did not quote her directly in the portion that has been reported.In practical terms, the pay cut means the guard accepted less than the most he could have been paid. The $20 million is the gap between that ceiling and the extension.Curry says the family sees it his way.He also shrank the question. People ask whether a decision like this stressed him out, Curry said, and his answer leaned on gratitude and understanding. The figures in the NBA, from team valuations to the salary cap to max deals, can feel unreal, he admitted. “'Oh, you stressed out about the decision,' and all that–the gratitude and understanding, the numbers we're talking about, and of course there's team valuations and the salary cap, max numbers and all,” the Warriors veteran shared.Curry started with the odd economics of the league, moved to his first contract, then to his family, and finished on the court. Each step came back to what he can control.To explain how he thinks about money, Curry went back to the beginning. His first contract was worth $44 million, at about $11 million a season, and he said this decision traces back to it. “It goes back to my very first contract, the $11 million, the four for $44 million that I signed.You sign contracts based on information that you have and what you feel like is right.”A player signs a contract based on the information available and on what feels right at the time, he said. The instinct behind that first signing is the one he cites now. By that standard, the extension is one more call made with the facts he has.The destination is just as clear in his words. Curry said he wants to stay with the Golden State Warriors and close this chapter the right way, with his family sharing that outlook.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry explains how Ayesha Curry reacted to the $20 million pay cut. Curry ties the Warriors extension to his first NBA contract, worth $11 million a season. Curry said he wants to stay with the Golden State Warriors and close this chapter the right way.

Twitch streamer Reginald “Reggie,” also known as “Lil Rodney Son,” says he is done streaming on Twitch after a fallout involving Kai Cenat. He’s blackballing people, right?”Reggie’s comments came during an ongoing dispute with Kai and members of the Clover Boys.He has made several allegations involving Kai in recent days, including claims connected to RaKai. NEW DELHI: India have moved into the top five of the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a stunning day of gold-medal performances across sports.India now have 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals, taking their overall tally to 76 medals. They are currently fifth in the standings, behind China, Japan, South Korea and Uzbekistan.China continue to lead the medal table with 162 gold, 81 silver and 73 bronze medals, for a total of 316 medals. The victory gave India their first Asian Games women's hockey gold medal in 44 years. It also secured a direct berth for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Lalremsiami scored the all-important goal in the 10th minute with a superb tomahawk strike. India then defended their lead brilliantly to hold on for the gold.Sujeet Kalkal added another gold for India in the men's 65kg wrestling category after a dramatic final. The Indian wrestler defeated Tajikistan's Abdulmazhid Kudiev 10-9 after trailing 2-9 at one stage.Kudiev made a strong start and prevented Sujeet from attacking in the opening period with his arm locks. But once Sujeet understood his opponent's style, he used his speed and technical skills to turn the bout around.He scored eight points in a row and completed the comeback with a decisive takedown with around 20 seconds remaining.Sujeet then held on to his one-point lead to clinch the gold.Indian boxers also enjoyed a memorable day, winning three gold medals.Lovlina Borgohain won the women's 75kg title, while Parveen Hooda clinched gold in the 65kg category. Both teams scored 54 points in the first set and 56 in the second before India pulled away to secure the gold.

Article Title: Grandmother’s gift, a second-hand bow and three Asian Games medals: How 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod made history
Article Text:

Coach saw the potential early

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

2026: The breakthrough year

From a Rs 3,000 wooden bow to Asian Games history, Kumkum Mohod’s rise has been built on sacrifice, discipline and an unwavering belief in her ability. At just 17, the Amravati archer has emerged as one of the brightest young stars in Indian archery after winning two gold medals and a silver at the 2026 Asian Games.Kumkum’s golden run in Aichi-Nagoya began with the women’s recurve team event, where she teamed up with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma to defeat South Korea 5-2 and help India win its first-ever Asian Games gold in the event. She then combined with Dhiraj Bommadevara to claim silver in the mixed recurve team event. On Saturday, she completed a remarkable campaign by defeating South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in the individual recurve final, winning the shoot-off 10-8. The victory made Kumkum the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games, and that medal was gold.The individual title also secured one of the quota places for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The quota belongs to the country rather than the individual athlete, but for Kumkum, it represents another major milestone barely months after breaking into the senior international circuit.Kumkum’s story began in Amravati, Maharashtra, in 2018. Her mother, Rupali, noticed a relative’s daughter practising archery at coach Prafull Dange’s academy and encouraged Kumkum, then a schoolgirl, to give the sport a try.Her first bow was a basic wooden one bought with Rs 3,000 given by her grandmother. Within six months of taking up the sport, Kumkum had won a silver medal at the sub-junior nationals, an early sign that she could go a long way in the sport.Her family, however, had limited financial resources. Her father, Anil Manohar Mohod, made cardboard boxes for sweet shops and bakeries in Amravati. As the family struggled with the costs of training and travelling for competitions, he often took Kumkum to events on his motorcycle rather than pay for transport.Even after she reached the international stage, Kumkum continued to compete with relatively modest equipment. The bow she used to help India win women’s recurve team gold at the Archery World Cup in Shanghai earlier this year was second-hand and had already been used by her for five years.Kumkum’s coach Prafull Dange has been with her for around eight years and has repeatedly highlighted her discipline and willingness to learn. Dange said he was impressed by her stubbornness to improve, along with her upper-body strength and shoulder position. During the Covid-19 pandemic, when normal training was disrupted, the pair worked extensively on short-distance shooting. According to Dange, those drills helped Kumkum strengthen her back muscles and improve her drawing technique.The 2026 season changed Kumkum’s profile completely. She helped India win women’s recurve team gold at the Archery World Cup Stage 2 in Shanghai, marking India’s first women’s team gold in the event since 2021. She later added another World Cup gold in mixed recurve with Dhiraj Bommadevara in Antalya.Those performances earned her a place in India’s Asian Games squad. She arrived in Aichi-Nagoya as the youngest member of India’s recurve squad but quickly showed that age was no barrier.She won her first two individual matches 6-0 before progressing through the knockout stages. In the quarterfinal, she defeated reigning world champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4. She then beat China’s Jingyi Zhu 6-2 in the semifinal to book her place in the final and secure the Olympic quota place for India.At 17, she has already become a World Cup gold medallist, an Asian Games champion and an Olympic quota-earner.
Article Summary: Kumkum Mohod won two gold medals and a silver at the 2026 Asian Games. The 17-year-old is the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games, and that medal was gold. The individual title also secured one of the quota places for India at 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Kolkata: Gurinder Singh Sangha, a Jalandhar-based international hockey umpire and technical official who was appointed by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) as umpire manager for the hockey competition at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, has left Japan before the tournament concluded following multiple complaints of alleged sexual misconduct against him.Sources alleged that Sangha misbehaved with a female hockey official from Malaysia.“A Malaysian official has complained that he tried to hug and kiss her in the name of mentoring, and he has had to leave the Asian Games in Nagoya midway, Hockey India leadership is having conversations about starting an investigation,” said a Hockey India official.The HI official said the latest allegations had once again raised questions about Sangha's conduct and the handling of earlier complaints against him.Meanwhile, Asima Ali, Hockey India vice-president and executive member, welcomed the development.“There can be no tolerance for any form of sexual misconduct in sport. The message has to be clear that complaints will be taken seriously and acted upon promptly. We must be stern in our dealing with such offenders and ensure that the sport remains a safe environment for everyone,” said Ali.Multiple sources also alleged that Sangha, who has previously officiated at major events, including the Asian Games, Olympic qualifiers and the Asia Cup, behaved inappropriately with a member of the hotel staff and showed her obscene videos in his room.The latest complaint is not the first allegation levelled against Sangha. During the Hockey India League in Ranchi in January 2025, a female umpire filed a formal complaint against him while he was serving as Umpires' Manager. Hockey India subsequently confirmed receipt of the complaint and constituted a three-member committee to conduct a preliminary investigation into the matter.According to the complaint, the umpire alleged that Sangha's conduct during an interaction at the team hotel in Ranchi on January 20, 2025, was "unwanted and inappropriate" and left her uncomfortable.In a communication dated Jan 21, 2025, Bhola Nath Singh, secretary general of Hockey India, informed stakeholders that a three-member panel had been constituted in consultation with the federation's Internal Complaint Committee for Prevention of Sexual Harassment to carry out a preliminary investigation and submit its report within two days.The latest episode comes amid increased scrutiny of misconduct complaints within Indian hockey. Earlier this year, Hockey India removed a support staff member from a national camp after harassment allegations surfaced against him, stating that action had been taken immediately after the matter came to its notice.The federation has also grappled with other complaints in recent times, including an April 2026 complaint alleging sexual harassment and abuse of authority by a Hockey India official, and a 2025 case involving misconduct allegations against a junior women's team coach.During the inaugural Women's Hockey India League, a coach was also removed overnight after authorities were informed of harassment complaints involving younger players.

Article Title: Parveen Hooda holds her nerve to clinch Asian Games boxing gold in 3-2 thriller
Article Text:
India's Parveen Hooda (PTI Photo)

Lovlina ends India's 12-year wait

Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women's 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games , beating Chinese Taipei's Chen Nien-Chen 3-2 in a split decision in a closely fought final.The Indian boxer had to dig deep in the deciding round after Chen levelled the contest following two rounds. Parveen held her nerve in a tense finish, relying on her counter-punching as the Chinese Taipei boxer pressed for the decisive blows.The victory adds another boxing gold for India on a day when Lovlina Borgohain also stood atop the podium.Parveen made a cautious start to the final, with both boxers initially keeping their distance. She found success with her counters before stepping in with combinations, including some effective body shots. The judges awarded her the opening round 5-0.Chen responded in the second round. Parveen continued to use her reach and movement to keep her opponent at bay, but Chen found her range with quick 1-2 combinations and landed enough clean punches to take the round 10-9 on all five cards.With the scores level heading into the final round, Chen came out aggressively and landed a couple of early jabs.Parveen weathered the pressure and began finding openings with quick combinations of her own.The Indian then switched to counter-punching as Chen pushed forward in the closing stages. The strategy proved enough to edge the contest, with Parveen winning the final by a 3-2 split decision.The gold marks a significant turnaround for Parveen, whose medal from the Hangzhou Asian Games was revoked following a doping violation. She had also exited the 2026 Commonwealth Games at the quarterfinal stage.Chen, a former world champion, came into the final as the 2026 Asian Championships gold medallist and had also won bronze at the previous Asian Games and the Paris Olympics.Earlier on Friday, Lovlina Borgohain ended India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final.The Olympic bronze medallist secured a 5-0 unanimous decision to upgrade the silver medal she won at the previous edition, giving herself a gold medal on her birthday.Lovlina became only the second Indian woman after MC Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold. Mary Kom had claimed the 51kg title at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain ends India's 12-year wait for an Asian Games women's boxing gold by defeating China's Ziyi Bao in the women's 75kg final. Parveen Hooda completed a remarkable comeback by clinching the women’s 65kg boxing gold at the Asian Games.
