MUMBAI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Friday, questioning his repeated references to his past as a tea seller.In a video posted by news agency IANS, Dipke said, "This person is just travelling around the world with our money. One thing is that he keeps saying, 'I have sold tea, I have sold tea, I have sold tea.' Why did you sell tea? Did we ask you to sell tea? We said you could have gone to school, studied, and got a job."Dipke also quipped, "PM Modi's fashion sense and skin care is on point. Even the big actors, models cannot match his style."The CJP founder was addressing thousands of people who gathered at Shivaji Park despite Mumbai Police denying permission for the protest.The demonstration was held to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Dipke also accused Delhi Police Deputy Commissioner of Police Sachin Sharma of being close to Union home minister Amit Shah while referring to the police action during the separate Delhi protest."Some police officers were telling me that this Sachin Sharma is a Sanghi. He is Amit Shah’s favourite. So I want to tell Sachin Sharma: if you are a Sanghi, wear khaki shorts (RSS uniform), don’t wear the police uniform!" he said.Dipke also said the turnout at Shivaji Park would overwhelm the barricades put up by the authorities."So many people will arrive that your barricades won’t be enough!" Dipke said.The CJP has demanded Kumar's resignation, criminal proceedings against him, a freeze on the SIR exercise and restoration of the January 2025 voter list.The protests followed a report in The Indian Express that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period on matters involving electoral rolls, voter registration and the Commission's technology systems.The Election Commission has rejected suggestions of an internal rift and maintained that decisions taken by the poll panel, including those relating to SIR, were unanimous and had the approval of all three commissioners.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had earlier urged Mumbaikars to join the protest and accused Kumar of being a "traitor" and the "real anti-national"."The youth of the whole country, the young generation, everyone came out last time for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan. And this time too, it is going to be the same with Gyanesh Kumar, who is a traitor to the country. The youth of Mumbai are hitting the streets again. Today, a massive protest is going to happen at Shivaji Park. And I want, I appeal to all the Mumbaikars and our friends. Everyone come," Das said.Veteran actor Shabana Azmi and singer Vishal Dadlani were among those who addressed the gathering, while actor Naseeruddin Shah and other public figures also joined the protest.Azmi said the demonstration was about democracy, people's rights and the right to vote."This is a question of our democracy. It is a question of our rights. It is a question of our voice. We have been told since childhood to cast our votes, claim our rights, and raise our voices. But when our fundamental right is snatched away or manipulated, what is a person supposed to do?""Naturally, they will protest, and this "people's power" is unstoppable now. Once the spark is lit, you can see how it spreads; it is happening all across India...The names of thousands upon thousands of people have been removed from the lists...After today's protest, we will see if action is taken or if we have to keep fighting this battle. We have to fight the battle for as long as it takes," Azmi said.Dadlani said the issue should concern supporters of all political parties if the election system was compromised."I would say this is extremely important. You may support any political party, but if the country's election system itself is compromised, then the country and democracy will no longer survive.""So, I would tell everyone, even those who support the BJP, that they too are with us and are part of this country. So I would tell them as well: wake up. Remove Gyanesh Kumar, reverse this entire process, eliminate the SIR, and protect every citizen's right to vote," Dadlani said.The CJP demonstration was also met by a counter-protest by a group identifying itself as "Gen Next Mumbai".One counter-protester accused Dipke and others of speaking about dismantling the Constitution and said the group had gathered to defend it."People like Abhijeet Dipke speak of dismantling the Constitution. Today, however, we stand beneath the statue of Babasaheb Ambedkar because we know how to protect and respect the Constitution. That is why we have gathered here for a peaceful demonstration; the conduct of the Cockroach Janata Party will not be tolerated," the protester said.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis also hit back at the protesters, saying allegations against the Election Commission had already been countered."The entire matter has been exposed. Following the press conference held by the three Election Commissioners, their fake narrative has been busted. Yet, attempts are still being made to push this fake narrative. They will not succeed in this," Fadnavis said.In Delhi, opposition leaders and youth organisations staged a demonstration near Jantar Mantar against the Election Commission and demanded Kumar's removal. Police had denied permission for the protest and imposed restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused the government and the Election Commission of undermining people's voting rights and said opposition leaders were prepared to face arrest."This is for saving the democracy of the country, saving the vote for a common man. Common men's votes are snatched by Modi and Shah through the Election Commission of India. So, this is a do-or-die fight for the Congress party and the INDIA alliance and all other opposition parties. We are not going to allow this thing," Venugopal said.Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also backed the protests, saying thousands of young people were exercising their constitutional rights and demanding Kumar's resignation."Today is Gandhi Jayanti. And today, thousands of young people are on the streets against vote theft - peacefully, without violence, exercising their constitutional rights. Their demand is clear: Gyanesh Kumar must resign. Save democracy," Gandhi said in a post on X.BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said protests were legitimate but protesters had to follow prescribed rules and obtain permission."In any democratic system, holding protests is absolutely legitimate, but there are certain rules and procedures to follow. Permission must be obtained, and people can protest wherever they want within the prescribed rules. Our country is democratic, so anyone can protest. However, if the rules are not followed, people may be detained. Detention during protests is, in any case, a common occurrence," Alok said.The protests come amid an ongoing political dispute over the Election Commission's handling of SIR and allegations concerning electoral rolls. The Election Commission has maintained that its decisions on SIR were taken unanimously.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questions PM Modi's past as a tea seller. Demonstration held to demand resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. CJP has demanded Kumar's resignation, criminal proceedings against him, a freeze on the SIR exercise.

Article Title: Woman convicted of killing 10-year-old held in Delhi after 20 years in hiding
Article Text:
She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. (AI Image)





NEW DELHI: For more than 20 years, Sadhana managed to live away from prison where she was to serve a life sentence. A life convict in a kidnapping-murder case of a 10-year-old boy, Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005.Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar.The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point. Police said witnesses Jagdish Chand and Vasdev had seen Sadhana holding his hand while crossing GT Road around 5.30pm. Sadhana and co-accused Raj Kumar were arrested from Jahangirpuri.The two were living together and the child’s father, Balwant Ram, and his family had objected to it. A previous dispute led to resentment and a decision to take revenge, police said.During the trial, Sadhana was found to be the last person seen with the child. Police said she had also concealed Kumar’s presence at her house and played an active role in the conspiracy. She was convicted under sections 302 (murder), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder) and 120B (criminal conspiracy) of IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.Sadhana was lodged in Tihar Jail on Jan 9, 1990.After spending years in jail, Sadhana was released on parole on Dec 27, 2005, which was extended by three weeks on medical grounds. She, however, did not surrender on Jan 18, 2006, and began a second life.She changed her name to Pooja and moved through different places to avoid detection. Police said her final parole was arranged by another Raj Kumar, a Tilak Nagar resident, on the reference of Janki, a woman who was lodged with Sadhana in jail. Sadhana stayed with him before taking up a job at a private company in Noida.There, she met Keshav, a carpenter. They moved to Mukundpur, where they lived for around five years before shifting to Haridwar. Police said Sadhana married Keshav in a temple and used his name as her husband in documents, helping conceal her identity.Meanwhile, investigators continued to pursue leads through intelligence, old associates and family links. A recent lead about a woman living under an assumed identity took a team to Haridwar and Sadhana was arrested on Sept 27. Her years of borrowed independence came to an end as she was sent back to jail.
Article Summary: Sadhana went missing after walking out on parole in Dec 2005. Over the years, police said, she changed her name, moved cities and built a new life as Pooja. Last week, Delhi Police ’s crime branch arrested her in Haridwar. The case dates back to Jan 6, 1990, when the boy went missing from Azadpur T-point.

India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. The 17-year-old defeated South Korea’s Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off to become the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. Her victory also secured an Olympic quota place for India for the 2028 Los Angeles Games.Pranavi Urs also scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win individual golf gold at the Asian Games, while helping India claim silver in the women’s team event alongside Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team events.On October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold. The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India then added three more gold medals in boxing and wrestling, with Parveen Hooda winning the women’s 65kg title, Ankush Panghal taking gold in the men’s 80kg category and Sujeet Kalkal winning the men’s freestyle 65kg event.The Indian women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold by defeating China 1-0 in the final, with the victory also securing a direct qualification spot for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.On October 3, Kumkum completed a memorable Asian Games campaign by winning individual recurve gold. After being pushed to a shoot-off by Oh Yejin, the 17-year-old held her nerve to shoot a 10 and beat the South Korean 8, securing India’s first individual women’s recurve gold at the Asian Games.Pranavi Urs added another historic gold in golf. The 23-year-old became the first Indian woman to win an individual golf gold medal at the Asian Games. She also helped India win silver in the women’s team event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing, archery and golf.The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. India also collected silver medals in sailing and archery, with Prince Noble Kurisinkal and Manu Francis finishing second in the men’s skiff.Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara lost to China in the mixed recurve final, while Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge finished runners-up to South Korea in the men’s recurve team event.The latest addition came in golf, where Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar won silver in the women’s team event. Article Title: A self-funded centre keeping Gandhian flame alive in Marathwada
Article Text:
Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: A building in the Silk Mill Colony of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has been quietly keeping the Gandhian thought alive for both younger and older generations.Known as the Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan, the hub serves as a critical reference point for students, activists, and researchers seeking to explore Gandhian literature, khadi spinning, and the core concept of Sarvodaya—the welfare of all.Dnyanprakash Modani, the 77-year-old Gandhian thinker, who started the full-fledged centre to coincide with the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi in 2019, said that the principles and methods of Gandhiji can still strongly appeal to modern audiences if they are presented through a contemporary lens.“With its inclusive approach, our centre brings together Gandhians under one roof, making it one of the few surviving spaces for non-violent, secular, and democratic discourse in the region,” he said.A full-panel pictorial exhibition titled ‘Mohan se Mahatma’, tracing the journey of Mohandas to the Mahatma, is one of the highlights of the centre.“The evolution of Gandhiji from a commoner into a towering personality revered as the ‘Mahatma’ itself sets off a journey of inner transformation for many.Our exhibition has captured the key moments of his life,” Modani said.The list of activities at the centre is long and diverse. It regularly conducts Sutkatai Prashikshan, which is training in spinning on the charkha—the symbol of self-reliance. It also runs classes in music, painting, sculpture, acting, and other arts. For students who have dropped out of the formal education system, the centre provides special educational support to bring them back into mainstream education. It also offers career guidance and counselling for school and college students.For those interested in deeper study, the centre conducts Grantha Shikshan, which includes study circles on the life and works of Gandhi, Phule, Ambedkar, and saint literature. To propagate the life, work, and philosophy of Gandhiji, it organises lectures, study classes, residential camps, and seminars, while also creating new literature. Its Sujana-Sajag Nagarik Abhiyan is a campaign to create aware, sensitive, and constitutionally committed citizens in the light of Gandhian thought. Besides, the bhavan is also known as the main organiser of the city-level Gandhi jayanti celebrations on Oct 2 at the Mahatma Gandhi statue in Shahganj.Notably, the establishment is entirely self-financed without a single rupee of govt grants, foreign funding, or even public donations—perhaps making it the only such institution in the country.“At a time when Gandhian institutions are struggling, it is our honest attempt to ensure the father of the nation does not remain only in history books, but becomes a living method of personal and social change,” Modani said.He added, “Great scientist Albert Einstein famously said that future generations will scarcely believe that a man like Gandhiji ever walked the earth. As one of our goals, we endeavour to raise our collective understanding of society so that people will actually understand what the words of Einstein mean.”
Article Summary: The Mahatma Gandhi Sarvodaya Bhavan in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is a hub for Gandhian thought. It is run by 77-year-old Dnyanprakash Modani, who started the centre to coincide with the 150th birth anniversary of Gandhi in 2019. It organises lectures, study classes, residential camps, and seminars, while also creating new literature.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: 16 years after construction, KDMC mayor finally moves into civic bungalow
Article Text:
The bungalow was constructed in 2010.





KALYAN: Sixteen years after it was constructed, the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s (KDMC) new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant, with mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performing the vastu shanti puja and entering the bungalow on Wednesday.The bungalow was constructed in 2010. However, a dispute over access to the property kept the residence largely unused for years. Several mayors subsequently attempted to resolve the road issue, but the efforts failed as villagers whose land was required for the access road were reportedly unwilling to part with the land.Even after the civic body spent lakhs of rupees on repairs, the bungalow remained unused. Former mayor Vinita Rane had performed a puja at the residence but chose not to stay there.With prolonged neglect, wooden furniture inside the bungalow was damaged and several portions were affected by termites. The civic administration later undertook extensive repairs to make the premises habitable again.After taking charge as mayor in February, Thavil took up the long-pending access issue. As she travels daily from Titwala to Kalyan, she personally held meetings with villagers and discussed their concerns. Following the resolution of the issues, the access road was finally constructed, paving the way for the mayoral residence to be used.After the road was made accessible and the neglected bungalow was completely repaired, Thavil finally entered the Adharwadi residence on Wednesday, bringing an end to the 16-year wait for the civic property to be put to its intended use.
Article Summary: Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant. Mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performed the vastu shanti puja and entered the bungalow on Wednesday.

Article Title: 'I stayed out of water to avoid tan': Pune teen who escaped death at Diveagar beach
Article Text:
Soham Gore, a student who didn't enter the water of Diveagar beach on the fateful evening of Oct 1





PUNE: Soham Gore, a Std XI student, escaped the Diveagar beach tragedy in which eight students drowned after he chose not to enter the water.“I get tanned easily and I don’t like the way the humidity makes me feel sticky, so I did not enter the water. Otherwise, I could have also drowned,” Soham said on Friday, as he attended the funeral of his close friend Pranav Bansode in Alandi, visibly shaken by the tragedy.“Pranav was very excited about the trip and wanted to see all the places. He was brilliant in studies and wanted to become an engineer. We have been friends since Std VI. I will miss him terribly,” Soham said.Soham was among the 42 students — 25 boys and 17 girls — who had gone on a trip to Raigad district. It was organised by private coaching institute Winners Academy and Study Centre in Alandi.Recounting the terrible day, Soham said the students gathered in the temple town around 3am on Thursday. A private bus carrying the students and teachers — two men and four women — left around 3.30am.“We reached Raigad Fort around 7am. Since the ropeway was closed, we trekked to the fort. We spent a few hours there and visited several historic spots,” he said.After lunch at a private hotel near the foothills of the fort, the group went to Diveagar beach around 4pm.“We were all excited. But I had a bad experience while swimming at a beach earlier as my face had become badly tanned. So, I decided not to enter the water,” Soham said.“Three of my friends also stayed out. We sat on a stone structure near the beach and were enjoying ourselves while the others entered the sea.”Soham said the girls remained closer to the shore while several boys ventured further into the sea. Some teachers also entered the water with the students.“They were happily playing in the water. After about 20 minutes, we suddenly saw the teachers running out and screaming for help,” he said, and added: “Initially, we could not understand what was happening. Then, we became scared and realised that something was seriously wrong.”Local residents and police personnel reached the beach quickly and rescued several people. But they were unable to save eight students, all 16 years old and from Alandi and neighbouring villages.“The bodies were brought out within half an hour. CPR was administered and they were taken to hospital in ambulances. We were taken to a hotel in the bus,” Soham said.Another student, Sarthak Chaudhari, lost his cousin Tanmay Vahile in the tragedy.“Tanmay died in front of my eyes and I could not do anything. I am still in shock. The incident keeps playing on my mind. I cannot forget the fun moments we had together,” he said.Parents who gathered at the Alandi crematorium said several students had been traumatised by the incident and were struggling to cope. Some were crying continuously and some others were not even eating, they said.“Some are in deep shock and are not in a position to narrate the incident,” a parent said.
Article Summary: Soham Gore, a Std XI student, escaped the Diveagar beach tragedy in which eight students drowned after he chose not to enter the water. Soham was among the 42 students — 25 boys and 17 girls — who had gone on a trip to Raigad district. The students gathered in the temple town around 3am on Thursday.
